questions.question: Why does a Spring Boot JAR need only Java on the server and no separate web server?
options: It uses the operating system's built-in web server
It has an embedded server such as Tomcat inside the JAR
The database acts as the web server
questions.explanation: Spring Boot packs an embedded server into the executable JAR, so java -jar is enough to serve requests.

questions.question: Which is the recommended way to change settings between test and production without rebuilding the JAR?
options: Edit the compiled classes on the server
Build a separate JAR for every server
Use profiles, environment variables and command-line options
questions.explanation: Build once and steer the same JAR from outside with profiles, variables and command-line options.

questions.question: application.properties has app.welcome=Dev. application-prod.properties has app.welcome=Live. The JAR starts with --spring.profiles.active=prod and no other setting. What is the value of app.welcome?
questions.explanation: The active profile file overrides the same property in application.properties.

questions.question: app.welcome=Dev is in application.properties. The app starts with the variable APP_WELCOME=Hello set and no profile. What is the value of app.welcome?
questions.explanation: Spring Boot maps APP_WELCOME to app.welcome, and environment variables beat values in application.properties.

questions.question: A JAR built with java.version 21 fails on the server with 'UnsupportedClassVersionError'. What is the most likely bug?
options: The server runs an older Java than the one used to build
The port is already in use
The JAR has no main method
questions.explanation: That error means the classes were compiled for a newer Java than the runtime. Install Java 21 on the server.
